name: Queen's Gambit
summary: 1.d4 d5 2.c4: White offers the c-pawn to pull Black's d-pawn away from the centre. It is not a true gambit: after 2...dxc4 White wins the pawn back. The plans are pressure on d5, a central pawn majority, and the minority attack.

white: Pressure d5: c4, Nc3, Bg5 to pin the f6 knight, and cxd5 at the right moment.
In the Accepted, win the pawn back calmly with e3 and Bxc4.
In the Carlsbad structure, push the b-pawn to b4 and b5 (the minority attack) to leave Black a weak c-pawn.
Keep the e4 break in reserve: when it comes, White's centre is complete.
black: Hold d5 with ...e6 (Declined) or ...c6 (Slav), or give it with ...dxc4 and hit the centre with ...c5.
Free the cramped position with ...dxc4 and ...Nd5, or with the ...c5 and ...e5 breaks.
Solve the light-squared bishop: in the Slav it comes out to f5 before ...e6.
Look for tricks against a loose bishop on g5: the Elephant and Cambridge Springs traps.

structures.name: Carlsbad: after cxd5 exd5
structures.text: White has pawns on a2, b2, d4 and e3 against a7, b7, c6 and d5. White's queenside pawns are fewer, but b4 and b5 attack c6 and leave Black with a weak pawn: the minority attack. Black's counterplay is on the kingside with ...Ne4 and ...f5.

structures.name: Isolated queen's pawn
structures.text: A d-pawn with no neighbours is a weakness in the endgame, but in the middlegame it gives space and the e5 square for a knight. The side with the pawn attacks; the other side blockades on d5 and trades pieces.

white: g5 bishop: pins the f6 knight and adds pressure on d5.
c3 knight: the third attacker of d5.
c1 rook: on the half-open c-file in the Orthodox lines and the minority attack.
Light-squared bishop: d3 aiming at h7, or c4 after it wins back the pawn.
black: e7 bishop: breaks the pin on f6 and guards the king.
d7 knight: supports the ...c5 and ...e5 breaks and the f6 knight.
c8 bishop: the problem piece in the Declined; free it with ...dxc4 and ...e5.
Queen: a5 in the Cambridge Springs, e7 after trades on e7.

lines.name: Declined, Orthodox: Capablanca's freeing line
lines.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O 6. Nf3 Nbd7 7. Rc1 c6 8. Bd3 dxc4 9. Bxc4 Nd5 10. Bxe7 Qxe7 11. O-O Nxc3 12. Rxc3 e5

notes.1.d4: Takes the centre with a pawn that the queen already guards.
notes.2.c4: Attacks d5. If Black takes, White plays e3 and wins the pawn back with a bigger centre.
notes.2...e6: The Declined: d5 stays, but the c8 bishop is shut in.
notes.4.Bg5: Pins the f6 knight, a defender of d5.
notes.7.Rc1: The rook takes the c-file before it opens.
notes.8...dxc4: Black waits until the bishop has moved, then takes, so the bishop moves twice.
notes.9...Nd5: Capablanca's freeing manoeuvre: trade pieces to ease the cramped position.
notes.12...e5: The freeing break: now the c8 bishop sees the kingside.

lines.name: Exchange Variation: the minority attack
lines.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. cxd5 exd5 5. Bg5 c6 6. e3 Be7 7. Bd3 Nbd7 8. Qc2 O-O 9. Nf3 Re8 10. O-O Nf8 11. Rab1

notes.4.cxd5: White fixes the pawn structure: the Carlsbad.
notes.5.Bg5: Pins the knight and develops before Black can play ...Bf5.
notes.8.Qc2: Controls f5 and h7, so ...Bf5 is not possible.
notes.10...Nf8: The knight heads for g6 or e6 to guard the kingside.
notes.11.Rab1: Prepares b4 and b5: the minority attack against c6.

lines.name: Queen's Gambit Accepted: win the pawn back
lines.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 dxc4 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. e3 e6 5. Bxc4 c5 6. O-O a6 7. dxc5 Qxd1 8. Rxd1 Bxc5

notes.2...dxc4: Black gives up the centre for a while and plans to hit d4 with ...c5.
notes.4.e3: Opens the bishop's diagonal to take back on c4.
notes.5.Bxc4: The pawn is back. White has more central influence.
notes.5...c5: The counter: Black attacks d4 at once.
notes.6...a6: Prepares ...b5 to gain space with tempo on the bishop.
notes.7.dxc5: White trades queens with a small lead in development.
notes.8...Bxc5: Material is level; White's pieces are a little quicker into play.

lines.name: Slav Defence: the bishop gets out first
lines.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 dxc4 5. a4 Bf5 6. e3 e6 7. Bxc4 Bb4 8. O-O O-O 9. Qe2

notes.2...c6: The Slav: d5 is held without blocking the c8 bishop.
notes.4...dxc4: Now Black takes, planning ...b5 to keep the pawn.
notes.5...Bf5: The point of the Slav: the bishop is out before ...e6.
notes.7...Bb4: Pins the c3 knight and slows e4.
notes.9.Qe2: Prepares e4 to take the centre.

traps.name: Elephant Trap: the pin on f6 is not real
traps.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Nbd7 5. cxd5 exd5 6. Nxd5 Nxd5 7. Bxd8 Bb4+ 8. Qd2 Bxd2+ 9. Kxd2 Kxd8

notes.4...Nbd7: It looks as if d5 now has too few defenders.
notes.6.Nxd5: The mistake: White takes a pawn, counting on the pin of the f6 knight.

traps.punishment: 6...Nxd5 gives up the queen: 7.Bxd8 Bb4+ 8.Qd2 Bxd2+ 9.Kxd2 Kxd8 and Black is a piece up. The f6 knight was free to take because the check on b4 wins the queen back with interest. Play 6.e3 and develop.

traps.name: Lasker Trap: promoting to a knight
traps.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e5 3. dxe5 d4 4. e3 Bb4+ 5. Bd2 dxe3 6. Bxb4 exf2+ 7. Ke2 fxg1=N+ 8. Ke1 Qh4+

notes.2...e5: The Albin Countergambit: Black gives a pawn to drive a wedge to d4.
notes.4.e3: Natural, but it lets the d4 pawn come forward with tempo.
notes.6.Bxb4: The mistake: White takes the bishop and forgets the pawn.

traps.punishment: 6...exf2+ 7.Ke2 fxg1=N+ promotes to a knight with check, and after 8.Ke1 Qh4+ Black is winning. White had to take the dangerous pawn first with 6.fxe3.

traps.name: Cambridge Springs: the loose bishop on g5
traps.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Nbd7 5. e3 c6 6. Nf3 Qa5 7. Nd2 Bb4 8. Qc2 O-O 9. Bd3 dxc4 10. Nxc4 Qxg5

notes.6...Qa5: The Cambridge Springs: the queen pins the c3 knight and watches the fifth rank.
notes.7...Bb4: Pins the c3 knight a second time.
notes.9.Bd3: The mistake: it lets ...dxc4 open the fifth rank with tempo on the bishop.

traps.punishment: 9...dxc4 hits the d3 bishop and opens the fifth rank, so the queen on a5 now attacks the g5 bishop. White cannot save both: 10.Nxc4 Qxg5 wins a piece. 9.Bh4 or 9.Be2 keeps everything guarded.
